text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired PD-987654: Multiple canary instances returning 429 after rollout v2026-03-15-09

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-987654 created. Trigger: canary-5xx-or-429-rate > threshold. Notified: oncall@redwood. Escalation policy: 10m -> lead-sre.

mira: I'm oncall, picking this up. can anyone paste the first failing log?

alex: seeing token-bucket denies on the embedder side. here's a slice from canary-3 (tail -n 60):

```
2026-03-15T09:03:12Z canary-3 embed-serving WARN request_id=44a2 rate_limit=exceeded status=429 model=embed-v2 seq_len=1
2026-03-15T09:03:13Z canary-3 embed-serving WARN request_id=44a3 rate_limit=exceeded status=429 model=embed-v2 seq_len=3
2026-03-15T09:03:14Z canary-3 kvcache INFO cache_hit=false
```

jen: same metrics from the autoscaler/ratelimiter dashboard — qps per instance spiked ~2.5x post-rollout. Looks like the new model variant increases token-per-request cost unexpectedly.

ryan: confirm — model v2026-03-15 pulls in a larger tokenizer, embedding batcher changes; we accidentally removed a batching optimization. that could increase per-request token ops and trigger local ratelimit buckets.

mira: pagerduty, ack?

pagerduty: Incident PD-987654 acknowledged by mira (oncall). Escalation timer paused.

mira: ok plan: 1) pause the rollout 2) reduce traffic to canaries (traffic diversion to stable) 3) if traffic still sees >5% 429s for 5m, rollback. jen/ryan, can you prepare rollback steps?

ryan: preparing. rollback command is `rdctl rollout undo release/2026-03-15 --to-revision=2026-03-14`. also we can immediately change routing via feature-flag: `flare set release-traffic release/2026-03-15 0.0`

alex: I'm going to try a temporary ratelimit increase on the service to buy time. patching nginx ratelimit key_quota to 2x for canary group.

infra-bot: Applying config patch to stack/canaries/ratelimit: set quota=2000 -> success (job id: j-84b2).

mira: runbook step: execute traffic diversion now. I'll do the feature-flag change and monitor.

mira: `flare set release-traffic release/2026-03-15 0.05` -> returns: updated. (reducing canary traffic to 5%)

jen: telemetry shows immediate drop in 429 rate on canary-1 and canary-2, canary-3 still noisy (~3.2% 429s). overall platform 429s fell from 3.6% -> 0.9% after diversion.

alex: nginx patch showed partial mitigation, but the underlying token ops are still high. I'm packaging a hotfix to restore batching; if we can't stabilize within 10m we should rollback.

mira: pagerduty note: we're keeping this P1 for now, customer impact limited (small % of requests). notify support to watch for tickets. @support-team please standby.

pagerduty: PD-987654: Escalation scheduled in 10m if no update.

mira: status update: hotfix attempt failed in canary-3 due to build mismatch. initiating rollback to previous revision now. executing: `rdctl rollout undo release/2026-03-15 --to-revision=2026-03-14 --confirm`

ryan: rollback in flight. watching orchestration.

infra-bot: Rollback job j-84b3 started: rolling back 3 canaries -> stable revision 2026-03-14. Estimated completion 2m per shard.

alex: logs show 429s trending down as old revision warms.

jen: telemetry: platform-wide 429s back to baseline 0.2% within ~6m of rollback start. canary error budget now healthy.

mira: closing the loop — I've updated PagerDuty: PD-987654 status = resolved (mitigated via rollback). Adding follow-up: postmortem + deploy checklist update.

pagerduty: PD-987654 resolved by mira (oncall). Duration: 00:18:40.

mira: action items: - assign postmortem to ryan/alex/jen - add pre-rollout perf smoke to CI (token-cost check) - fix missing batching optimization and re-run canary in staging before release.

ryan: assigning in issues: ISSUE-2053 created and linked.

alex: I'll draft a short blameless postmortem and include logs + graphs.

jen: I'll add a temporary alert rule to detect sudden per-instance token op increases.

mira: thanks team. I'll hand back to normal channel monitoring in 10m. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Incident channel will remain pinned for 1h for follow-ups.

mira: final note for support: customer-facing statement template posted in #support-ops.

mira: thread closed for active mitigation. postmortem to follow within 48h.
